title: Proposal store: nothing reaches the queue without the owner's approval
objective: Add a `proposal` table (id, project_id, source, rationale, spec JSON holding a list of task specs, status pending|approved|rejected, created_at, decided_at) plus `nc proposals`, `nc proposal <id>` (full text of the proposed tasks), `nc approve <id>` and `nc reject <id> "<reason>"`. Approving inserts the proposed tasks as queued tasks exactly as `nc task --file` would; rejecting stores the reason and creates nothing. This is the gate that keeps a planner from filling its own queue: the planner in a later task will only ever write proposals.
acceptance: $ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
$ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
$ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m nc.cli --home /tmp/nc-prop-check proposals
A test asserts that a pending proposal creates no task rows, that approve creates exactly the proposed tasks with their acceptance criteria intact, and that reject creates none and keeps the reason
Approving the same proposal twice does not duplicate the tasks
The schema change is applied by the existing migration mechanism so an existing state.db keeps working
boundaries: Only touch nc/state.py, nc/cli.py, README.md and files under tests/
Do not add an agent role and do not change the scheduler in this task

title: Owner inputs that wake the planner: nc feedback and nc plan
objective: Add `nc feedback "<text>"` (optionally --project, --task) storing the text as a message of a new kind `feedback` addressed to the planner, and `nc plan <project> [--note ...]` requesting a planning pass. Both must create-or-wake a single planner agent per project (role `planner`, state runnable) so the existing timer picks it up on its next tick; neither may start a session itself. `nc status` should show pending feedback so a note is never silently lost.
acceptance: $ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
$ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
A test asserts that feedback followed by plan leaves exactly one runnable planner agent for that project and both messages in its inbox
A test asserts feedback for an unknown project exits non-zero without writing anything
Neither command runs an agent session
boundaries: Only touch nc/state.py, nc/protocol.py, nc/cli.py, README.md and files under tests/
Do not implement the planner turn itself here

title: Planner role: turn feedback and repository state into a bounded proposal
objective: Teach the scheduler to run agents of role `planner` and add its prompt to nc/roles.py. Its brief carries the project, the repository layout, open feedback, the currently queued/blocked tasks, and the last accepted tasks; its only permitted product is one proposal written via the outcome file (a `proposal` outcome field holding a list of task specs in the same shape as tasks/neocortex-pool.json), or ASK. It must not edit files, must not create tasks, and must propose at most 5 tasks per turn. Its model comes from config models['planner'] and defaults to the heaviest configured model.
acceptance: $ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
$ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
A scripted-adapter test asserts a planner turn creates a pending proposal and zero tasks, and that the tasks appear only after nc approve
A test asserts a proposal of more than 5 tasks is rejected as a protocol failure rather than silently truncated
A test asserts the planner brief contains the open feedback and the existing queued tasks
The planner runs with the model from config models['planner']
boundaries: Only touch nc/roles.py, nc/protocol.py, nc/scheduler.py, nc/config.py, README.md and files under tests/
Do not give the planner a worktree and do not let it commit

title: Keep the planner from eating the queue
objective: A planning pass must be triggered, never spontaneous, and must not starve real work: the scheduler picks planner agents only when no worker or critic is runnable, refuses to run one when the project already has more than 10 queued tasks or a pending proposal, and records how many planner turns each project has spent. Add these limits to config (planner_max_queued, planner_max_pending_proposals).
acceptance: $ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
$ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
A test with a runnable worker and a runnable planner asserts the worker runs first
A test asserts a planner with a pending proposal for its project is skipped and the run ends idle rather than looping
A test asserts the queued-task ceiling is enforced
boundaries: Only touch nc/scheduler.py, nc/config.py, README.md and files under tests/

title: Onboard the two real projects as separate namespaces
objective: Add `nc onboard <project-id> <git-url>` which clones the repository under /root/projects/<id>, registers it with its detected test command, and creates a single queued reconnaissance task for it whose only product is a written REPORT.md in the worktree describing build, test entry points and the three most valuable improvements — no source changes. Onboard aiscreeps and airogue this way; their tasks must never mix with neocortex tasks.
acceptance: $ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
$ /root/neocortex/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
A test onboards a local throwaway repository and asserts the project row, the clone and exactly one queued task scoped to that project id
A test asserts task ids stay per-project and nc tasks --project shows only that project's tasks
Re-running onboard for an existing project updates it instead of failing
boundaries: Only touch nc/cli.py, nc/state.py, README.md and files under tests/
Do not clone the real repositories from the test suite
